reasons.D: Tower sergeant: a quartered blue-and-cream torso and a cream cross on the cap crown, the clearest heraldic family read from the high camera (second critic 7.35, first; first critic 7.18, second).
reasons.F: Gatewarden: a crested sallet, cream-edged pauldrons and a big brass chest roundel, the brief's heraldic, sturdy, honest garrison met most fully (7.30, second; first critic's top set at 7.55).
reasons.A: Militia: a wide steel kettle-hat brim over a blue coat and a cream baldric, a distinct top-down outline and a believable town watchman (7.00, third; up from 6.85).

fixes.D: Give the charcoal pauldrons a blue face with cream or brass edging and add the missing brass badge.
fixes.F: Widen the plume into a blue-and-cream front-to-back crest or blue the helm crown so the head reads from the ARPG camera.
fixes.A: Put cream or town-blue heraldry on the pauldron tops and the hat crown so the town colours read before the steel.

notes: 6 of 6 survived the draft (g01 exited 1 but its set passed, so no resume) and 6 of 6 survived the rework. Both critics put D, F and A in the top three, though not in the same order. The common weakness: heraldry sits on the chest front, where the high camera never looks; the pauldron tops and helm crown should carry the town colours. B and C drift into iron with grey slab pauldrons.
